transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Devin Holt (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (CISO - Sapphire), Tom Breuer (Cloud Architect), Nadia Ortiz (Compliance), Raj Patel (DevOps), Ellen Soo (Legal)

Summary: Quick posture readout for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope, discussion of Trust Center access pattern, KMS integration options (cloud KMS vs HSM), audit log retention and schema, and data residency mapping. Agreed next steps around evidence sharing and a technical KMS diagram and policy.

Topics: SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 scope, Trust Center read-only access, RBAC and SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit log exports, KMS/HSM integration, data residency EU/UK, redaction and evidence packaging.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a posture readout and then get into the KMS conversation. we have about 45 minutes.
[00:07] Aisha Khan: Great, thank you. we just want to make sure the controls mapping matches our internal SOC 2 work and that we can get access to the trust center artifacts without exposing sensitive customer data.
[00:16] Marco Reyes: Yep, we'll walk through both. quick note — our trust center link is a read-only portal, we can provision scoped accounts and audit them via SSO. there's also a redacted SOC 2 archive we can share.
[00:28] Tom Breuer: When you say SSO, are you supporting SAML 2.0 with SCIM for user provisioning? we need automated deprovisioning.
[00:36] Marco Reyes: Yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM are supported. some customers use just SAML with their IdP, others also enable SCIM. deprovisioning events are logged to the audit trail.
[00:45] Raj Patel: On the KMS side, important question — do you integrate with our existing AWS KMS and external HSMs? we need key separation for customer data.
[00:53] Marco Reyes: We support BYOK patterns. we can integrate with AWS KMS and wrap keys with an HSM-backed CMK. there's a couple of ways — either Redwood holds wrapped keys in the control plane or you keep keys only in your VPC via our private deployment option.
[01:05] Nadia Ortiz: For the SOC 2 auditors, we need explicit evidence of key management procedures and of who had access to key material. do you provide key access logs?
[01:13] Marco Reyes: Yes, KMS access events are exported to the audit logs. note — there may be some slight naming differences in the audit events, sometimes the product reports 'kms-call' or 'key-usage' in the logs; we can correlate.
[01:24] Aisha Khan: Also, what's the retention on audit logs? we typically need 2 years for certain evidence buckets.
[01:29] Devin Holt: Default retention is 90 days in the hosted plan, but for Dedicated or Private deployments you can configure longer retention and export to your SIEM (S3/Cloud Storage) for long-term archive. we'll include the retention promises in the SLA appendix.
[01:43] Ellen Soo: From legal perspective, we need to confirm data residency commitments in writing. Our regulated datasets must stay in- region.
[01:50] Lina Park: Absolutely. we map region policies to workloads. for example EU customers can pin to eu-west-1 region and restrict model routing. we also have private deployment for air-gapped or VPC-only needs.
[02:03] Tom Breuer: What's the process for evidence access? do auditors get their own accounts or do we pull bundles?
[02:09] Marco Reyes: We usually do redacted bundles for initial review and provide auditor read-only Trust Center accounts for on-site or remote review, depending on your preference. auditors can be scoped so they only see control documentation and test artifacts, not production logs with customer PII.
[02:22] Raj Patel: A small nit — sometimes the Trust Center exports have different file naming conventions which made mapping harder in our last audit. is that something you can standardize?
[02:29] Devin Holt: Yes, we can provide a packaged evidence zip with a mapping csv. we'll add consistent naming for item IDs to help your compliance team ingest them.
[02:39] Aisha Khan: On encryption: do you support envelope encryption? how is the key lifecycle tracked?
[02:44] Marco Reyes: Envelope encryption model is supported. we track key versions and rotation events in the audit log. rotation is configurable — some customers do 90 days, others 1 year. we can show sample rotation policies.
[02:55] Nadia Ortiz: For ISO27001 scope, we need to know which subservices are in scope — e.g., hosted API vs dedicated pools vs private installs. can you confirm the scope and provide the ISO certificate and scope doc?
[03:05] Lina Park: We'll share the ISO27001 cert and a scope PDF. quick disclosure — our hosted API includes the control plane and the managed model serving; dedicated pools provide data isolation but require committed capacity, and private installs are out-of-the-box for fully customer-managed infra.
[03:19] Tom Breuer: For the private deployment option, are audit logs forwarded to our own log collector or do you store copies? we want primary custody in our environment.
[03:27] Marco Reyes: In private deployments you manage the exporters; we ship a forwarding agent that posts to your endpoint, so primary custody is yours. hosted by Redwood will keep canonical logs but you can request that we forward copies to your S3.
[03:40] Raj Patel: Regarding RBAC, do you support fine-grained roles for model-level access? we want developers to have generate-only rights and ops to have config rights.
[03:48] Marco Reyes: Yes, role-based access control includes per-route and per-model permissions. we also support token scoping so keys can be limited to embedding-only or generation-only.
[03:58] Aisha Khan: Can we get a sample role matrix? that'll help map to our internal control matrix.
[04:02] Lina Park: We'll include a role matrix sample in the package.
[04:06] Ellen Soo: One more legal question — do you support encryption of customer data at rest with our customer-managed keys where Redwood never sees the plaintext key?
[04:14] Marco Reyes: With private deployment yes. For hosted we have BYOK where you provide a CMK and we only receive wrapped keys; operationally there are still wrapped keys held in the control plane but plaintext never leaves your KMS/HSM. We'll have the cryptographic flow diagram in the KMS doc.
[04:30] Tom Breuer: Any known incompatibilities with requirement for FIPS 140-2 HSM?
[04:34] Marco Reyes: We can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs; some connector work is needed on the customer side for the FIPS endpoint. we'll call that out in the diagram.
[04:45] Nadia Ortiz: About evidence packaging, can we request a redaction pass for screenshots/logs to remove other customers' identifiers?
[04:52] Devin Holt: Yes, we have a redaction workflow and can perform a manual pass for auditor bundles. there is a small SOW for bespoke redaction if needed.
[05:02] Aisha Khan: Okay good. let's align on specific deadlines. we'll want the redacted SOC 2 and ISO scope by early next week to give to our auditor.
[05:10] Lina Park: Understood — I'll upload the redacted SOC 2 type II and ISO scope by Monday. Marco will send the KMS/HSM diagram and sample IAM policy. Devin will provision a Trust Center read-only account and share onboarding steps.
[05:22] Raj Patel: One operational detail — when KMS key rotation happens, are there brief windows where tokens could fail? how do you handle cache invalidation, KV cache was a pain point for us before.
[05:31] Marco Reyes: We coordinate rotations with rolling update semantics and a key rollover window. there's an automatic rewrap path for cached tokens. sometimes logs refer to 'kv cache' as K V cache which is a transcription artifact in our docs, we'll make sure to use consistent nomenclature.
[05:45] Tom Breuer: Can you also include a mapping between SOC control IDs and where evidence lives in the Trust Center? that would save a lot of time.
[05:52] Marco Reyes: Absolutely — we'll include a control mapping CSV and a sample mapping dashboard screenshot.
[05:58] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. from a risk perspective anything outstanding we should be aware of?
[06:03] Lina Park: Only the items we've flagged — residency confirmation, HSM endpoints for FIPS, and the naming consistency for evidence exports. none are blockers for procurement.
[06:12] Ellen Soo: We'll also circulate a short list of legal questions and required contract language around data processing and audit rights.
[06:18] Lina Park: Great. quick recap and next steps?
[06:21] Devin Holt: Recap: Redwood to share redacted SOC2 and ISO scope, SE sends KMS diagram/IAM policy, CSM provisions Trust Center account, customer provides residency list. We'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for the KMS design the week of 9/28 if that works.
[06:37] Aisha Khan: Week of 9/28 works for us for a deep dive focused on HSM and audit log formats.
[06:42] Lina Park: Perfect — we'll send calendar invite. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example/trustcenter/sapphire-readonly (provision link), https://redwood.example/trustcenter/evidence-packages (redacted zip examples), internal KMS diagram placeholder: /docs/kmsschema-v1.pdf
